claims.text: Sweden public broadcaster SVT stated that with 50% of the votes counted, the two main political blocs were separated by only 20,000 votes.
Projected results from Sweden's election authority gave Magdalena Andersson's Social Democrat-led left-wing bloc a one-seat majority over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's coalition.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson promised cabinet jobs to the hard-right Sweden Democrats if he remains in office.
Partial election results suggest the Sweden Democrats lost support for the first time since entering parliament in 2010.

Magdalena Andersson asked after voting: "Should we have a government entirely dominated by the Sweden Democrats, something that has never happened in Sweden before? Or should we have a government led by me, which will steer Sweden in a new spirit of co-operation?"
The Sweden Democrats were founded by Nazi sympathisers in the 1980s.
SVT's projection at 9:45pm local time showed the opposition bloc leading the government parties by 175 seats to 174 seats.

Projected vote shares showed Social Democrats at 27.6%, Moderates at 20.0%, Sweden Democrats at 17.5%, Left Party at 8.2%, Centre Party at 7.1%, Christian Democrats at 6.3%, Green Party at 6.2%, and Liberals at 5.5%.
Sweden Democrats leader Jimmie Åkesson acknowledged his party lost percentage points compared to 2022 and likely lost its status as Sweden's second-largest party.
Christian Democrats leader Ebba Busch stated that the election result may remain uncertain until Wednesday.
Liberal Party leader Simona Mohamsson called her party's election results "a historic comeback".
Sweden is a Nordic nation with a population of 10.6 million people.
Swedish Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard stated that election results might not be clear until Wednesday when overseas votes arrive.
Under Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, Sweden abolished permanent residency for refugees, tightened welfare rules, and increased expulsions.
While voting in Rinkeby, Sweden Democrats leader Jimmie Åkesson remarked that the suburb "doesn't look like Sweden".
Voting took place in Sweden in a closely fought election that could bring the far-right into government.
Six people died and 107 were rescued after the passenger ferry Virgo Transport 8 capsized in the Java Sea.
At least 130 people were reported missing after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 ferry during bad weather.
The Virgo Transport 8 ferry carried 213 passengers and 30 crew members.
The Virgo Transport 8 ferry departed Surabaya at 10:33 on Saturday and was scheduled to reach Banjarmasin at 14:00 on Sunday.
Indonesian government data shows 111 ship accidents were recorded between 2020 and 2026.
France 24 reported at least one person died and more than 100 people remained missing after a ferry carrying 243 people sank between Java and Borneo.
Indonesian Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi stated that helicopter surveillance confirmed the Virgo Transport 8 had capsized but had not sunk as of 3pm local time.
Search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana reported rescue vessels were battling waves up to 2.5 metres high.
A speedboat carrying eight people, including five journalists, went missing near Mount Anak Krakatau in Lampung province.
The 119-metre Virgo Transport 8 ferry was built in Japan in 1987 and was operated by PT Virgo Karya Shipping.
The Virgo Transport 8 ferry was carrying 89 vehicles in addition to passengers and crew.
A passenger ferry fire in the Philippines four days prior killed at least 76 people with 10 others missing.
The Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office received a report two hours after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 at about 2am Sunday.
A Russian strike hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border.
Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and former CIA Director David Petraeus were at the Yagodyn border station nearby around the time of the attack.
US President Donald Trump urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, citing US diesel prices exceeding $6 a gallon.
Moscow banned diesel exports in July after Ukrainian long-range strikes targeted Russia's oil and gas industry.
Ukrzaliznytsia reported a Russian jet-propelled drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train at Yahodyn after an evacuation order was issued 15 minutes earlier.
Ukrzaliznytsia stated that a diplomatic train carrying Boris Johnson and European security advisers departed Yahodyn earlier than scheduled due to real-time timetable changes.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha characterized the strike near the Polish border as "Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and Nato".
Former Swedish Prime Minister Carl Bildt stated that passengers on his train were instructed to prepare for evacuation before safely arriving in Dorohusk, Poland.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned following an emergency meeting that he expects Russia to escalate the war in coming weeks.
Russia's Defence Ministry stated its strikes targeted railway infrastructure used to transport European military cargo.
A strike hit a truck less than one kilometre from the Polish border, briefly halting operations at the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing.
Rosatom head accused Ukraine of striking fuel trucks near the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power station.
A Ukrainian drone strike on Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan killed at least two people and injured several others.
Overnight Russian attacks using over 450 drones and missiles killed at least six people across Ukraine, while Ukrainian air defenses intercepted 405 drones and four missiles.
Brent crude futures rose $3.62 to $108.23 per barrel following strikes on Saudi Arabia and ships in the Gulf.
WTI crude futures rose $3.15 to $103.20 per barrel.
Negotiations scheduled in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states were postponed.
An attack on an Iranian commercial cargo vessel off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz killed one person and wounded four others.
UKMTO reported a severe fire broke out on a vessel after it was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz.
Approximately one-fifth of world oil and LNG supplies passed through the Strait of Hormuz prior to the outbreak of war on February 28.
Muscat proposed in July a joint regional mechanism splitting control of the Strait of Hormuz 50-50 between Oman and Iran.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi announced on X that the regional meeting in Salalah was postponed "in the interests of consensus".
Iranian state media quoted a foreign ministry official stating the postponement of the Salalah meeting was a joint decision by Tehran and Muscat requested by some regional countries.
Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Saudi Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
S. Jaishankar and Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud discussed Houthi militant attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.
Iraq stated that recent attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory.
The United States defeated France 97-79 in Berlin to win its 12th Women's Basketball World Cup.
France led the US by two points at halftime before the US outscored France 30-12 in the third quarter.
Breanna Stewart scored a game-high 22 points, while Jackie Young scored 18 points for the US.
Caitlin Clark scored 12 points for the US in the final after scoring one point in the semifinal.
Gabby Williams scored 16 points in the first half and four points in the second half for France.
Spain won the bronze medal at the Women's Basketball World Cup by defeating Germany 81-58.
The US extended its unbeaten run at the Olympics and World Cups to 20 years while securing its fifth consecutive World Cup title.
France earned silver in its maiden World Cup final appearance.
France opened a 14-point lead early in the second quarter following a 21-2 run.
The US has not lost a Women's Basketball World Cup match since 2006, extending its streak to 36 consecutive wins.
Spain point guard Iyana Martin scored 20 points and recorded nine assists in the bronze medal match.
